stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Sweep the three sliders (angle of incidence $i$, barrier tilt $\alpha$, wavelength $\lambda$) and watch how the reflected plane wave leaves the barrier. Advance when each slider has covered at least half of its range.
stages.concept: A plane wave reflects off a straight barrier so that the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence, both measured from the barrier normal. The wavelength $\lambda$ is preserved during reflection — only the direction changes.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: A target reflected direction $r^*$ is drawn as a dashed orange arrow. Adjust $i$ and $\alpha$ until the reflected wavefronts propagate along that direction. Wavelength does not affect direction — it only changes the wavefront spacing.
stages.concept: The barrier's normal makes an angle $180° + \alpha$ with the $+x$ axis (screen frame, clockwise). Reflecting the incident propagation vector across the normal yields the reflected direction $r = 180° + 2\alpha - i$.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The reflected wave is hidden. Only the incident direction, the barrier and the target arrow remain. Compute an $(i, \alpha)$ pair that produces $r^*$ on paper, then set the sliders and submit. One try per setup — a miss rotates you to a new target.
stages.concept: Inverse formula: $i = 2\alpha + 180° - r^*$. Pick any convenient $\alpha$ in $[-30°, 30°]$ that keeps $i$ inside $[20°, 70°]$, then read off $i$. Wavelength is irrelevant — leave $\lambda$ anywhere.

labels.tip1: sweep every slider past half its range
labels.tip2: align the reflected wavefronts with the target arrow
labels.tip3: compute i and α on paper before touching the sliders
labels.peek_tip_anchor: Anchor: try α = 0 (barrier vertical). Then i = 180 − r*.

1.1: Which slider changes the reflected direction, and which one only changes the spacing between wavefronts?
1.2: Sweep each of i, α and λ to at least half its range. The stage advances automatically when all three coverage bits are lit.
1.3: Wavelength never changes the direction. If you're stuck on λ coverage, drag it end-to-end once — that's enough.

2.1: The orange arrow shows where the reflected wave should point. Start by matching the barrier tilt α, then fine-tune with i.
2.2: Lower i (steeper incidence) rotates the reflected direction farther from the barrier. Increasing α rotates both barrier and reflection clockwise.
2.3: Reflected direction (deg from +x on screen) equals 180 + 2α − i. Try α = 0 first and read off the required i.

3.1: The wavefront rendering is gone but the formula still holds. Write it on paper.
3.2: Formula: r = 180 + 2α − i. Choose α, then solve for i. Keep both inside their slider ranges.
3.3: Peek reveals the rearranged formula. Apply it directly to the target value shown by the r* label.
